relevance_note: Case report of a family with Alexander disease: the proband's "sequencing showed heterozygosity for the GFAP mutation c.1157A > G (p.Asn386Ser)"; her untested mother had MRI "suggesting a diagnosis of adult-onset AxD".
method_note: Built with a short Python script in the scratch directory; every span was located in the paper by script (only space/apostrophe variants normalised, then the exact paper text copied). Labels: 'the proband' is a role word, so the proband is 'patient' (rule 5) and her mother 'mother of patient' (rule 2). The previously published person in the Discussion with GFAP somatic mosaicism (cheek swab positive, blood negative) is included as 'ref [28] patient' because the paper gives a variant-level fact; no variant description is printed (variant_original_string 'not reported', zygosity 'mosaic'). People 'reported several times in patients with AxD [1, 2]' were not given rows (no individual-level detail). Table 1 (37 instances of published familial AxD from 22 studies) has only its caption in the Markdown; its contents are absent, so no rows were created from it. Neither patient's age at onset is stated as a number (proband presented aged 45 with an 8-month history; mother aged 71 with weakness over 4 years), so onset is 'not reported'. Mother was not genotyped (DNA could not be obtained); she has no variant row, and the proband's inheritance is 'not reported'. Possible contradiction: the proband's first MRI was 'reported as normal' locally, but on specialist re-review was 'concluded to be consistent with AxD'; recorded as an excluded row from the local report, with no specific checklist effect. Checklist: proband 'intermittent choking on food' recorded as a feature but not mapped to dysphagia; 'no sphincter disturbances' does not exclude the composite autonomic item; 'no cerebellar signs' with reported 'poor balance' left 'ataxia or cerebellar signs' not reported. Normal CSF, nerve conduction, EMG, sensory exam and pupils 'equal at 3 mm' recorded as excluded abnormalities (D-27). Pathogenicity is the authors' in-silico prediction ('predicted to be deleterious', CADD 23.3), not a functional assay.
